profile.name: John Tory
profile.ward: Mayor of Toronto (city-wide), December 2014 - February 2023; resigned February 17, 2023
profile.bio: John Tory served as the 65th Mayor of Toronto from December 2014 to February 2023, elected in 2014 and re-elected in 2018 and 2022. He resigned on February 17, 2023, after acknowledging a relationship with a staff member. A lawyer by training, he previously led the Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario (2004-2009), served as an MPP, worked as a broadcaster with CFRB, and held executive roles with Rogers Communications.
committees: Toronto Police Services Board (member by virtue of office)
Exhibition Place Board of Governors (member by virtue of office)

promises.text: Introduce a five-point housing plan: seek provincial authority for a 'use it or lose it' policy against idle developers, allow more missing-middle housing (laneway and garden suites) with development-charge exemptions for buildings of four units or fewer, create a Development and Growth Division as a one-stop development review shop, improve incentives for purpose-built rental housing, and grant a portion of city-owned land to non-profit developers.
Create 40,000 affordable rental units over 12 years (averaging about 3,300 per year), while keeping property tax increases capped at the rate of inflation or lower.

Advance a transit plan including a $586 million investment to add 60 new streetcars to the TTC fleet, launch the first RapidTO bus-only corridor on Eglinton East, introduce free two-hour TTC transfers and a Fair Pass discount for low-income riders, and maintain the TTC's large electric bus fleet.

expensesDetailSource.publisher: City Clerk's Office, City of Toronto
expensesDetailSource.note: Figures are the City's routine disclosure of constituency services and office expenses, shown as published, by category, from 2013. This is a separate publication from the annual remuneration reports in expenses.json, with a narrower scope — office spending only, not pay, benefits or staff salaries — and the two are never added together. Amounts shown as personal funds are the member's own money, as the City reports it. Invoice-level documents stay on the City's site; category amounts link to them.
